newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel army mistakenly wounds civilian in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israel army mistakenly wounds civilian in Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli troops critically wounded a Lebanese man in the Jewish state's south Lebanon occupation zone on Tuesday, when they mistook his vehicle for one belonging to guerrillas, an army spokesman said.
"A Lebanese civilian was critically injured this evening by an Israeli force on patrol in the eastern sector of the security zone in south Lebanon," the spokesman said.

He said the force opened fire on the civilian's vehicle in the mistaken belief that guerrillas were in it, because of what the Israelis perceived as "suspicious movements by the vehicle as it neared the Israeli patrol".
An earlier army report that the victim was a militiaman of Israel's client South Lebanon Army (SLA) was incorrect, he said.
The civilian was taken to hospital in Israel for treatment. His condition was not immediately known.

The pro-Iranian Hizbollah organisation has vowed to oust the Israeli force of some 1,000 troops from the zone they hold with the aid of 3,000 SLA soldiers. Israel carved out the zone in 1985 to curb cross-border guerrilla raids on the Jewish state.
